text:
For Aston Villa, a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was a triumph of sorts. The hard numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the Sunderland box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable too. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the only survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic just seven months ago.
With 90 minutes and 25 seconds showing on the big screens, Chemsdine Talbi almost snatched victory for Sunderland, the Moroccan winger shaving one of Zion Suzuki’s uprights with a spell-bending strike. Talbi did almost everything right, bursting past Aaron Wan-Bissaka and comfortably eliminating the defender before using Boubacar Kamara as a mannequin to get his bearings, but his curling right-foot shot was ultimately a few inches too close to a post. For Villa, a first clean sheet in the league here since March, but this draw extended their winless run to five matches.
For Sunderland, this may not have been the dopamine hit or high of beating Chelsea, but here was another gutsy showing, and without two key players in Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom were absent through injury. It was a big team performance, another feather in the cap of Jules Ahoka, the 20-year-old midfielder who shone on his first Premier League start. Ahoka started last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s second division. Noah Sadiki was omnipresent in midfield and Nordi Mukiele inspired at centre-back. Robin Roefs, too, made a couple of late saves, the first to tip over a speculative strike from Ross Barkley, among the raft of Villa substitutes, and another to prevent Mukiele from scoring a freakish own goal.
McGinn’s arrival on the hour provided an instant lift – on and off the pitch. The Villa captain cleverly slipped Alysson behind the Sunderland left-back, Reinildo Mandava, inside the right channel and from there the 20-year-old Brazilian squared the ball in search of Nicolas Jackson, who was lurking inside the six-yard box. Mukiele, however, cut the chain, brilliantly hacking the cross clear. Mukiele’s heroics did not stop Emery from asking questions of how his players did not seize on a rare opening. A few minutes later, McGinn sent a left-foot, first-time strike over the bar after instigating the move from the heart of midfield. Villa welcomed the Scotsman’s drive and industry.
Sunderland seemed content to soak up the Villa pressure, though it always felt a dangerous game as the hosts sought to dial up the pressure. Emery introduced the 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo, who trained with England Under-21s during the international break, from the bench but in place of Jackson rather than to join Villa’s club-record signing in attack. By which point Ibrahim Mbaye had entered and it was Mbaye and McGinn who combined to fashion another nearly-moment, but the latter’s cross from the left flashed across the box. Disbelief reigned in the stands, but had Talbi located the top corner, things could have felt a lot worse at the final whistle.
